title: At the table
subtitle: Serving and pairing Muscat
objectives: Pair each Muscat style with food
Know how long to keep them

steps.title: Match the style
steps.body: Dry Muscat suits asparagus, a classic in Alsace, and aperitifs. Moscato d'Asti suits fruit salads, panettone and light desserts, even brunch. Beaumes-de-Venise suits fruit tarts and melon. Rutherglen Muscat suits sticky toffee pudding, chocolate, coffee desserts and blue cheese.

steps.title: Service and age
steps.body: Serve Moscato d'Asti and dry Muscat at 6 to 8 degrees, sweet fortified Muscat at 12 to 16. Moscato d'Asti and dry Muscat are best within a year or two; their aroma fades. Fortified Muscats, already aged, keep for weeks once opened.

steps.explanation: Its toffee and raisin notes match rich desserts.

steps.body: Dry Alsace Muscat with white asparagus in spring is one of the few successful asparagus pairings.

steps.prompt: Moscato d'Asti is best drunk young.
steps.explanation: Yes. Its fresh grape aroma is its charm, and it fades with time.

steps.title: What you learned
points: Dry Muscat suits asparagus; Moscato suits fruit desserts
Rutherglen Muscat suits toffee and chocolate
Drink Moscato young; fortified Muscat keeps
